toc.title: Threats, VPC layout, traffic controls and private paths
Edge protection, detection, credentials, sign-in and external links

html:
1What You Will Learn

  • Design a VPC with subnets, route tables, security groups, network ACLs and NAT gateways
  • Choose a segmentation strategy with public and private subnets, and private paths to AWS services
  • Integrate Shield, WAF, Secrets Manager and sign-in services to secure applications
  • Pick the right detection service: GuardDuty, Inspector, Detective or Security Hub
  • Secure external connections with VPN and Direct Connect

2Threats, VPC layout, traffic controls and private paths

Running case

Lantern and Loom Locks the Shop

  • Bots scrape listings, and a flood of requests slowed the shop for an hour
  • A developer left SSH open to the whole internet
  • The database password sits in the source code
  • Customers need to sign in, and the team needs a private link to a partner's inventory system
  • Your job: close each door, one layer at a time

Threats and Defense in Depth

Layer Threat it faces Controls
Edge DDoS floods, SQL injection, scraping bots Shield, WAF
Network Open ports, unwanted traffic Subnets, security groups, network ACLs, Network Firewall
Workload Weak credentials, vulnerable software Roles, Secrets Manager, Inspector
Identity Stolen or shared logins IAM, Cognito, MFA
Detection Attacks already underway GuardDuty, Detective, Security Hub
  • Defense in depth: no single control is enough, so stack them

Exam tip: Match the threat to the layer first: floods and injection at the edge, open ports in the network.

A Secure VPC Layout

  • Public subnets: the load balancer and NAT gateway, with a route to the internet gateway
  • Private subnets: the application servers, with outbound access only through NAT
  • Isolated subnets: the database, with no route outside the VPC
  • Each subnet sits in one AZ; repeat the tiers in at least two AZs

Exam tip: Only what must face the internet goes in a public subnet; everything else goes in private ones.

Subnet Types and Route Tables

Subnet type Route to the outside Typical contents
Public A direct route to an internet gateway Load balancers, NAT gateways
Private No direct route to an internet gateway; uses a NAT device Application servers
Isolated No routes outside the VPC Databases
VPN-only A route to a VPN connection through a virtual private gateway Private office link
  • Every subnet has one route table (the main one by default) and one network ACL

Exam tip: What makes a subnet public is its route to an internet gateway, not its name.

Security Groups

  • A virtual firewall for the resources it is attached to, such as EC2 instances and load balancers
  • Stateful: return traffic for an allowed request is allowed automatically
  • Allow rules only: there is no deny rule, and traffic that no rule allows is blocked
  • A rule's source can be an IP range or another security group: chain load balancer, app and database tiers
  • Open SSH and RDP only to specific ranges, never to 0.0.0.0/0
  • Rules match protocols, ports and source; no additional charge

Exam tip: Security groups are the main control, and they can only allow.

Network ACLs

  • A network ACL allows or denies traffic at the subnet level
  • Stateless: a rule for inbound traffic does not allow the response, so allow return traffic too
  • Rules are numbered and evaluated from the lowest number; the first match applies
  • Rules can allow or deny
  • Every subnet has one network ACL; the default one allows all traffic
  • Best use: an extra layer, or a deny for a known bad address range

Exam tip: To block a specific address range, use a network ACL deny rule; a security group cannot deny.

Security Group or Network ACL?

Security group Network ACL
Applies to A resource's network interface A subnet
State Stateful Stateless
Rules Allow only Allow and deny
Evaluation All rules together In number order, first match
Default New group: no inbound, all outbound Default ACL allows all
Use it for Tier-to-tier access An extra layer; blocking ranges

Exam tip: Stateful, allow-only, on the resource: security group. Stateless, allow and deny, on the subnet: network ACL.

NAT Gateways and Outbound-Only Access [Verify live]

  • A public NAT gateway lets instances in private subnets reach the internet, but nothing outside can start a connection to them
  • It sits in a public subnet, has an Elastic IP address, and the private subnets' route table points to it
  • A zonal NAT gateway lives in one AZ: use one per AZ for resilience
  • A private NAT gateway links to other VPCs or on-premises networks; it has no Elastic IP
  • For IPv6, use an egress-only internet gateway
  • As of 5 November 2026: the docs also describe a Regional NAT gateway; check the page

Exam tip: Private servers that must reach out but never be reached: a NAT gateway in a public subnet.

VPC Endpoints: Private Paths to AWS Services

Endpoint type How it works Services
Gateway endpoint A route table entry; not PrivateLink S3 and DynamoDB
Interface endpoint Network interfaces with private IPs in your subnets, powered by PrivateLink Many AWS services, and your own or partner services
  • Traffic stays on the AWS network, not the public internet
  • An endpoint policy controls which principals can use the endpoint
  • Without an endpoint, service endpoints are public and reached through the internet gateway or NAT

Exam tip: Private S3 or DynamoDB access from a VPC: a gateway endpoint. Most other services: an interface endpoint.

3Edge protection, detection, credentials, sign-in and external links

Edge Protection with AWS WAF

  • AWS WAF is a web application firewall for HTTP(S) requests, at layer 7
  • Attach a web ACL to CloudFront, Application Load Balancer, API Gateway, AppSync or a Cognito user pool
  • Rules match IP addresses, headers, query strings, body or geography, and allow, block or count
  • Managed rule groups cover common threats such as SQL injection and cross-site scripting
  • Rate-based rules limit floods of requests from one source
  • A blocked request gets HTTP 403 or a custom response

Exam tip: SQL injection, scripting or bots against a web app: AWS WAF, on CloudFront or the load balancer.

DDoS Protection with AWS Shield

Shield Standard Shield Advanced
Cost Automatic, no extra charge Paid subscription
Protection Common network and transport attacks Expanded detection and mitigation
Extras None to set up Expert help; the subscription covers standard WAF fees for protected resources
Resources All AWS customers CloudFront, Route 53, Global Accelerator, load balancers, Elastic IPs
  • Attack classes: volumetric (layer 3), protocol (layer 4) such as a SYN flood, application (layer 7) request floods

Exam tip: Free and automatic: Standard. Extra protection, expert help and WAF fees covered: Advanced.

AWS Firewall Manager and AWS Network Firewall

Service What it does
AWS Firewall Manager Set protections once and apply them across accounts in Organizations, including new accounts and resources: WAF, Shield Advanced, security groups, network ACLs, Network Firewall
AWS Network Firewall A managed, stateful firewall and intrusion prevention service for a VPC; filters traffic at the VPC perimeter with Suricata-compatible rules, domain filtering and deep packet inspection
  • Network Firewall uses firewall endpoints in their own subnets; route tables send traffic through them

Exam tip: One policy for every account: Firewall Manager. Deep inspection inside a VPC's traffic path: Network Firewall.

Threat Detection: GuardDuty, Inspector, Detective and Security Hub [Verify live]

Service What it does
Amazon GuardDuty Threat detection from CloudTrail events, VPC flow logs and DNS logs; no agents for the base feeds
Amazon Inspector Scans EC2 instances, container images and Lambda functions for vulnerabilities
Amazon Detective Investigates findings: builds a behavior graph to find the root cause
AWS Security Hub One view of findings from GuardDuty, Inspector and Macie, plus checks against standards
  • As of 5 November 2026: the docs call the posture service Security Hub CSPM; check the name

Exam tip: Detect: GuardDuty. Scan: Inspector. Investigate: Detective. Aggregate: Security Hub.

Application Credentials: Secrets Manager and Parameter Store

Secrets Manager Parameter Store
Best for Secrets: database credentials, API keys, tokens Configuration: endpoints, AMI IDs, flags
Rotation Automatic, with a Lambda function None
Encryption Always, with KMS Optional (SecureString)
Cost Per secret and per call Standard tier free
  • Replace hard-coded credentials with a runtime call, allowed by the application's IAM role
  • For AWS access, use roles; for keys, KMS; for certificates, ACM

Exam tip: A secret that must rotate automatically: Secrets Manager.

Amazon Cognito for Application Users

  • User pool: a user directory that answers who is this user?; sign-up, sign-in, tokens, MFA, social, SAML and OIDC federation
  • Identity pool: answers what AWS resources may this user reach?; swaps a trusted token for temporary AWS credentials through STS; can serve guests
  • Use both for sign-in and direct access to services such as S3
  • A WAF web ACL can protect a user pool

Exam tip: Sign-in for customers: a user pool. Direct AWS access for those customers: add an identity pool.

Choosing the Sign-In Service

Who or what needs access Service
Employees to AWS accounts and AWS managed applications IAM Identity Center
Customers of a web or mobile app Cognito user pool
App users who need temporary AWS credentials Cognito identity pool
Windows or LDAP applications needing a directory AWS Directory Service
Servers and functions calling AWS IAM roles
Database passwords an app reads at run time Secrets Manager

Exam tip: Employees: Identity Center. Customers: Cognito. Code: roles.

Site-to-Site VPN and Client VPN

Service What it does Details
Site-to-Site VPN An IPsec connection between a VPC and your network Two tunnels per connection; AWS side is a virtual private gateway or transit gateway; your side is a customer gateway device
Client VPN A managed client-based VPN for individual users OpenVPN clients over TLS; sign-in with Active Directory, SAML or certificates; authorization rules

Exam tip: An office network to a VPC: Site-to-Site VPN. Individual remote users: Client VPN.

AWS Direct Connect

  • A dedicated network connection from your site to an AWS Direct Connect location, bypassing internet providers
  • Virtual interfaces: private (a VPC), public (public services such as S3), transit (transit gateways)
  • Gives consistent network performance
  • Not encrypted by default: add MACsec on supported connections, or run an IPsec VPN over Direct Connect
  • Build resilience with a second connection, or a VPN as backup

Exam tip: Private and consistent: Direct Connect. Private, consistent and encrypted: add a VPN or MACsec.

Choosing an External Connection

Need Choice
Quick, encrypted link over the internet Site-to-Site VPN
Consistent bandwidth and a private path Direct Connect
Private, consistent and encrypted Direct Connect with a VPN (or MACsec)
Individual remote staff Client VPN
High availability Two VPN tunnels; a second connection or VPN backup

Exam tip: Look for the words encrypted, consistent and individual users.

What the Exam Asks: Secure Workloads

  • Which network control: subnet type, security group, network ACL, NAT gateway or endpoint
  • Which edge service: WAF, Shield, Firewall Manager or Network Firewall
  • Which detection service: GuardDuty, Inspector, Detective or Security Hub
  • Which credential store: Secrets Manager or Parameter Store
  • Which sign-in or link: Cognito, Identity Center, VPN or Direct Connect

Exam tip: Name the threat or the traffic path first, then pick the layer.

4Design check, recap and practice

Design Check: Lantern and Loom Locks the Shop

Requirement Design
Bots and SQL injection against the storefront AWS WAF with managed and rate-based rules
A flood of requests slowed the shop Shield (Advanced for expert help)
SSH open to the world A security group limited to specific ranges
Block one hostile address range A network ACL deny rule
App servers need updates but no inbound traffic A NAT gateway in a public subnet
App servers read S3 privately A gateway endpoint
Database password in the code Secrets Manager with rotation
Customers sign in, upload photos Cognito user and identity pools
Private link to the partner Site-to-Site VPN, or Direct Connect with a VPN
  • Cover the right column, answer each row yourself, then compare

5Exam Q&A

5.1 Practice questions (choose the best answer; some ask for two)

S1Which TWO statements about security groups and network ACLs are correct? (Select TWO.)

  • ASecurity groups are stateful, so return traffic for allowed requests is allowed
  • BNetwork ACLs are stateful, so return traffic is always allowed
  • CSecurity groups support both allow rules and deny rules
  • DNetwork ACLs apply at the subnet level and can allow or deny
  • ESecurity groups are evaluated in rule-number order
Show the answer

Answer: A, D. Security groups are stateful and have allow rules only. Network ACLs are stateless, apply to a subnet, can allow or deny, and are evaluated in rule-number order.

S2Lantern and Loom's application servers run in private subnets. They must download operating system patches from the internet, and nothing on the internet may start a connection to them. What should the architect add?

  • AA route to an internet gateway in the route table of the private subnets
  • BA NAT gateway in a public subnet, routed from the private subnets
  • CAn Elastic IP address attached to every application server
  • DA network ACL rule that allows all inbound internet traffic
Show the answer

Answer: B. A public NAT gateway lets private instances reach the internet while blocking unsolicited inbound connections. A direct internet gateway route or public addresses would expose the servers.

S3Lantern and Loom sees a flood of unwanted requests from one known address range and wants to block it for every instance in a public subnet. Which is the simplest control?

  • AA security group rule that denies the address range
  • BAn IAM policy that denies the address range
  • CA route table entry that drops the address range
  • DA network ACL rule that denies the address range
Show the answer

Answer: D. A network ACL applies to the subnet and supports deny rules. Security groups have only allow rules, and IAM policies control API access, not network traffic.

S4Lantern and Loom's storefront runs behind an Application Load Balancer. It must be protected against SQL injection and against floods of requests from single IP addresses. Which solution fits?

  • AAn AWS WAF web ACL with managed rules and a rate-based rule
  • BAWS Shield Standard with custom SQL injection signatures added by the team
  • CSecurity group rules that inspect the body of every request
  • DAmazon GuardDuty configured to block malicious requests automatically
Show the answer

Answer: A. AWS WAF inspects HTTP(S) requests: managed rule groups cover SQL injection, and rate-based rules limit floods from one source. Shield protects against DDoS, security groups do not inspect request bodies, and GuardDuty detects but does not block.

S5Application servers in private subnets read product images from Amazon S3. Policy says this traffic must not cross the public internet or use a NAT gateway. What should the architect create?

  • AA VPC peering connection to the S3 service
  • BA second NAT gateway in every Availability Zone
  • CA gateway VPC endpoint for S3, with a route table entry
  • DAn internet gateway attached to the private subnets
Show the answer

Answer: C. A gateway endpoint adds a route that sends S3 traffic over the AWS network. Peering does not connect to a service, a NAT gateway uses the internet path, and an internet gateway exposes the subnets.

S6Lantern and Loom's code has the database password written in a configuration file. The team wants to remove it from the code and rotate it automatically on a schedule. Which service should they use?

  • AAWS KMS, to encrypt the configuration file
  • BAWS Secrets Manager, with automatic rotation
  • CA Parameter Store standard String parameter
  • DAn Amazon Cognito identity pool
Show the answer

Answer: B. Secrets Manager stores the credential, lets the application fetch it at run time and rotates it automatically. Parameter Store has no rotation, KMS manages keys, and Cognito handles application users.

S7Which TWO statements about AWS Shield are correct? (Select TWO.)

  • AShield Standard is provided automatically at no extra charge
  • BShield Advanced is provided automatically at no extra charge
  • CShield Advanced is a paid subscription that covers the standard AWS WAF fees of the resources it protects
  • DShield Standard blocks SQL injection by inspecting request bodies
  • EShield Advanced removes the need for security groups
Show the answer

Answer: A, C. Standard is automatic and free; Advanced is a paid subscription with expanded protection that also covers the standard WAF fees for resources it protects. SQL injection is a WAF matter, and Shield does not replace security groups.

S8Lantern and Loom wants to detect unusual API calls, contact with known malicious addresses and possible credential compromise across its accounts, without installing agents. Which service fits?

  • AAmazon Inspector
  • BAWS Config
  • CAmazon Detective
  • DAmazon GuardDuty
Show the answer

Answer: D. GuardDuty continuously analyzes CloudTrail events, VPC flow logs and DNS logs with threat intelligence. Inspector scans for vulnerabilities, Config records configuration, and Detective investigates findings after the fact.

S9Lantern and Loom's new mobile app must let customers sign in with a social account and then upload photos directly to an Amazon S3 bucket with temporary credentials. Which design fits?

  • AA Cognito user pool for sign-in and a Cognito identity pool for temporary AWS credentials
  • BAn IAM user for each customer, each with its own access keys
  • CIAM Identity Center with a permission set for customers
  • DOne shared IAM role whose keys are built into the app
Show the answer

Answer: A. The user pool authenticates customers, including social sign-in, and the identity pool exchanges the token for temporary credentials. IAM users and embedded keys are long-term credentials, and Identity Center is for the workforce.

S10A company needs a private connection to AWS with consistent network performance, and the traffic must be encrypted in transit. Which design meets both needs?

  • AAWS Direct Connect alone, because it encrypts traffic by default
  • BAWS Client VPN from each office computer
  • CAWS Direct Connect with a Site-to-Site VPN over it
  • DAn internet gateway with HTTPS only
Show the answer

Answer: C. Direct Connect gives a private, consistent path but does not encrypt traffic by default, so an IPsec VPN over it, or MACsec on a supported connection, adds encryption. Client VPN and the internet path are not consistent private links.

6Quick Reference Card

Topic Key fact
Layout public, private and isolated subnets across two AZs
Traffic security groups (stateful, allow) and network ACLs (stateless, allow and deny); NAT out, endpoints to AWS services
Edge WAF for web exploits, Shield for DDoS, Firewall Manager for every account
Detect and protect GuardDuty, Inspector, Detective, Security Hub; Secrets Manager for secrets
Access Cognito, Identity Center, VPN and Direct Connect
